states.name: Germany
timeline: Born in the parsonage at Röcken, Prussian Saxony, on 15 October
After his father's death the family moves to Naumburg
Boarding school at Schulpforta
University at Bonn, then Leipzig from 1865
Meets Richard Wagner in Leipzig on 8 November
Leaves for Basel and gives up his Prussian citizenship
Medical orderly in the Franco-Prussian War; falls ill with dysentery and diphtheria
The first Bayreuth Festival disappoints him
A summer at Tautenburg with Lou Salomé
The Jena asylum, then his mother's care in Naumburg from 1890
His mother dies; Elisabeth moves him to the Villa Silberblick in Weimar

events.title: Born at Röcken
events.text: Friedrich Nietzsche is born in the parsonage of Röcken, the son of the village's Lutheran pastor.

events.title: His father dies
events.text: Pastor Carl Ludwig Nietzsche dies after months of a brain illness; the boy is four.

events.title: Move to Naumburg
events.text: The widowed family moves to the cathedral town of Naumburg on the Saale.

events.title: Schulpforta
events.text: He wins a place at Schulpforta, Prussia's most famous boarding school for classics.

events.title: Student at Bonn
events.text: He enrols in theology and classical philology, and soon drops theology.

events.title: Schopenhauer
events.text: In a Leipzig second-hand bookshop he finds Schopenhauer's The World as Will and Representation.

events.title: Meets Wagner
events.text: At the house of Hermann Brockhaus in Leipzig he meets Richard Wagner; they talk of Schopenhauer.

events.title: Professor at 24
events.text: Basel appoints him professor of classical philology before he has a doctorate.

events.title: Tribschen
events.text: The first of many visits to Wagner and Cosima in their villa on Lake Lucerne.

events.title: Medical orderly
events.text: He trains at Erlangen and serves in the Franco-Prussian War, then falls gravely ill.

events.title: The Birth of Tragedy
events.text: His first book hails Wagner and the Dionysian spirit of Greek tragedy; philologists attack it.

events.title: Bayreuth foundation
events.text: He attends the laying of the foundation stone of Wagner's festival theatre.

events.title: First festival
events.text: The first Bayreuth Festival repels him: crowds, nationalism and his own illness.

events.title: Sorrento
events.text: A winter by the Bay of Naples with friends; his last meeting with Wagner.

events.title: Human, All Too Human
events.text: A book of sceptical aphorisms marks his break with Wagner.

events.title: He resigns
events.text: Migraines, vomiting and failing eyes force him to give up his chair.

events.title: The Engadine
events.text: His first summer in the high valley of the Engadine, at St Moritz.

events.title: Venice
events.text: Spring in Venice with his friend and copyist Heinrich Köselitz.

events.title: Genoa winters
events.text: The first of three winters in cheap rooms high above the port of Genoa.

events.title: Sils Maria
events.text: He discovers the village where he will spend most of his summers.

events.title: The rock at Surlej
events.text: By a pyramid-shaped rock on Lake Silvaplana, the thought of eternal recurrence comes to him.

events.title: Messina
events.text: A spring voyage to Sicily, where he writes light verses.

events.title: Lou Salomé
events.text: In Rome he meets the brilliant young Russian Lou Salomé; she refuses his proposal.

events.title: The Gay Science
events.text: God is dead, eternal recurrence and amor fati appear in one book.

events.title: Tautenburg
events.text: A summer with Lou in a Thuringian village ends in bitterness.

events.title: Zarathustra
events.text: At Rapallo he writes the first part of Thus Spoke Zarathustra in about ten days.

events.title: Wagner dies
events.text: Richard Wagner dies in Venice on 13 February.

events.title: Nice
events.text: His first winter in Nice; he will return for five winters.

events.title: Elisabeth marries
events.text: His sister marries the antisemitic agitator Bernhard Förster in Naumburg.

events.title: Beyond Good and Evil
events.text: Printed at his own expense, it sells very few copies.

events.title: Riviera earthquake
events.text: He lives through the earthquake that shakes Nice in February.

events.title: Genealogy of Morality
events.text: At Sils Maria he writes his history of master and slave morality.

events.title: Turin
events.text: He arrives in Turin and lodges by the Piazza Carlo Alberto.

events.title: Ecce Homo
events.text: In one autumn he finishes Twilight of the Idols, The Antichrist and Ecce Homo.

events.title: Collapse
events.text: On about 3 January his mind gives way; a horse story is told only years later.

events.title: Overbeck's rescue
events.text: His friend Franz Overbeck brings him from Turin to a clinic in Basel.

events.title: Jena asylum
events.text: He is admitted to the university asylum at Jena.

events.title: Mother's care
events.text: His mother takes him home to Naumburg and nurses him for seven years.

events.title: The Archive
events.text: Back from Paraguay, Elisabeth founds the Nietzsche Archive.

events.title: Villa Silberblick
events.text: After their mother's death, Elisabeth moves him to a villa above Weimar.

events.title: Death in Weimar
events.text: Nietzsche dies on 25 August, aged fifty-five.

events.title: Buried at Röcken
events.text: He is buried beside his father, by the village church where he was baptised.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's Germany, Switzerland, Italy and France, by what each country was to Nietzsche that year. A simplification: a whole country takes one colour, while the dots mark the exact places. Borders are today's; Germany was unified only in 1871, and Röcken and Naumburg were Prussian.
